## **Copper Monthly November 2011 No. 179** #### **Highlights** ##### **INSIDE THIS ISSUE** ###### **China might loosen its tight economic policies?** There were rumors saying the private high interest loans led to the flee of business owners and shutdown of their enterprises due to the breaking of the funding chain in private enterprises. Although enterprises couldn’t get loans from banks, they can use the form of trade financing. Under the current tight financial situation, the acceptance of enterprises couldn’t be discounted, therefore the former fund and operating mode are broken down, and the declining nonferrous metals prices deteriorates financing, so we believe it will spread to the copper industry. Inflation has become the focus in macro economy since H2 2010. Output gap has continued to decline for 18 months since Feb 2010, but began to fluctuate in recent 8 months and dropped again in recent 2 months. From the prospect of the lagged effects of conduction (output gap is usually 7 months ahead of CPI), inflation reached its peak in Q3 and would decline gradually after Q4. We noticed their relationship mode changed-the indicating function of output gap weakened, indicating that the driven force of CPI and competition was different during this period, and we judged this round of inflation wasn’t driven by demand, but if the inflation was triggered ###### **_Highlights_** China might loosen its economic policies?...1 ###### **_Copper Market Review_** Copper prices fluctuate at a wide rang…......2 Chinese refined copper imports rise in Sept 2011…………………………….……..............6 ###### **_News_** Sichuan Hongda to build 400ktpy refined copper project………………………..….………..…...8 Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Group to expand its refining capacity to 400kt………………....8 Xiangguang Copper listed on LME………...10 The market demand of the copper mine remains strong in 2011……..…..……………………..11 ##### **Statistics** Chinese Refined Copper Output by Region in Sept 2011……………….……..……………..14 Chinese Imports and Exports of Cu Products in Sept 2011………….………………..……......14 **_Market Data_** .…..……..……….…..….….....23 Website: www.antaike.com 1 Copper Monthly No. 179 by excessive currency, while the economic growth wasn’t stimulated by this reason, then it would contradict our common sense. We can ask what is the inner engine of China’s economic growth? We should re-think this. The liquidity has dropped to the normal level as China’s central bank had continued to conduct tight monetary policy. As the first year of the 12th Five-year Plan period, the declining economy must make the policy-

maker re-consider its monetary policies. 

Economic environment in China and abroad was still complex and faced a lot of uncertainties. Judged by the demand and supply relationship, demand of global nonferrous metals will continue to increase in 2012, and copper and aluminum and other main metals will have a stable production underpinned by growing demand. 

China’s macro economic policies will continue to be stabilizing in 2012, and a stable price will be the top priority in macro regulation. Further measures will be given to maintain a stable and rapid economic development, regulate economic structure and manage inflation, accelerate the transformation of development pattern so as to achieve a balanced and rapid economic development. 

It is now the key period in building a well-off society. Domestic demand for non ferrous metals continues to increase with the development of industrialization, urbanization and informatization, and the development of transportation, energy, affordable houses, infrastructure, and the build of a new countryside. The development of new strategic industries also provide strong support on nonferrous metal industry, besides, new environmental standards also require the industry to update its development mode so as to achieve new and higher goals. 

Production of nonferrous metals will continue to increase in 2012 due to the robust demand. And domestic price might be weaker than international market in 2012 due to the policies to curb inflation. Refined copper price might average at 69,000 yuan/t. 

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper prices fluctuate at a wide rang** 

Copper for three month on LME opened at US$6,910/t on Oct.3, and closed at US$8,175/t on Oct.28, touching a high of US$8,175/t on Oct.28 and a low of US$6,735/t on Oct.20. 

LME copper prices fluctuated at a wide range, with its closing prices falling below US$7,000/t for more than once. G-20 countries have reached an agreement on desirable resolution of the current European crisis on Oct. 27, which bolstered equities and resulting in about 6% of growth rate of LME 3-month copper prices. On the whole, the futures market is not stable. 

Copper for three month on SHFE was weaker than that on LME. Recent SHFE/ LME ratio was continuously decreasing. Copper for three month on SHFE opened at 55,060 yuan/t on Oct.10, and closed at 59,250 yuan/t on Oct. 28, touching a high of 59,250 yuan/t on Oct.28 and a low of 50,950 yuan/t on

###### **Chinese refined copper output has a m-o-m decline in Sept** 

Data released by China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association (CNIA) showed refined copper output was 457.60kt in Sept, down by 8% m-o-m or up by 18% y-o-y. The accumulative output from Jan to Sept was 3.93Mt, up by 15% y-o-y. According to statistics from Antaike, during Jan to Sept, output of 12 Chinese main refined copper producers produced 2.91Mt, up by 15% y-o-y. Of them, growth rate of cumulative refined copper output in Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Company, Shanghai Dachang Copper Co., Ltd, Jiangxi Copper Group, Jinchuan Group and Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Co. was 65.45%, 40.01%, 19.25%, 18.74% and 15.09% y-o-y and 14.17% respectively. While output of 12 Chinese main refined copper producers in Sept had a 0.81% m-o-m decline. 

Copper semis output reached 963.49kt in Sept., up by 3% m-o-m. The m-o-m increase of copper semis output was mainly because major domestic copper-using products outputs had a m-o-m rise in Sept., such as power generating equipment, AC motor, electric wire and cables. But the coming of off-season 

consumption in air conditioning and refrigeration industry will inhibit consumption at a certain degree in future. 

Copper-in-concentrate output was 111.18kt in Sept, slightly up by 2% m-o-m or by 15% y-o-y. The accumulative output from Jan to Sept was 919.21kt, up by 12% y-o-y. Analysis of data showed that copper-in-concentrate production of Jiangxi, Yunnan, Inner Mongolia, Anhui, Gansu, etc. as China’s top 5 regions for copper-in-concentrate production, increased by 20.08%, 8.55%, 4.00%, 6.45% and 27.11% during Jan to Sept. It is expected that relative good demand in Chinese copper market will further promote enthusiasm for production of domestic mine enterprises, as copper prices rebounding recently. It is estimated self-produced copper concentrate will maintain at a high level.

###### **Copper consumption** 

Because there was 7 holidays to celebrate China’s National Day, major domestic copper-using products output in Sept has not been released by National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS). So we can’t 

speculate copper consumption according to ending using products output of copper industry. According to Antaike’s research, power cable, as one of copper using large sectors, would still make great contributions to copper consumption in Sept. 

In addition, according to the statistics from China Electricity Council, during Jan-Sept investment in power source was 242.8 bln yuan, up by 5.1% y-o-y. Of investment in power source, investment in hydropower, th

ermal power, nuclear power and wind power were 63.5 bln yuan, 74.2 bln yuan, 53.2 bln yuan and 47.7 bln yuan respectively. Statistics from China Electricity Council still released that the newly added power generation capacity that has been put into operation in China was 49.62 GW in Jan to Sept, including 8.73 GW of hydropower, 32.95 GW of thermal power, 1.09 GW of nuclear power and 6.58 GW of wind power. Investment in power grid was 220.1 bln yuan, up by 11.3% y-o-y. newly built power substation capacity (above 220 kv) with capacity was 128,170,000 kva, with the length of 22,507 km. Refined copper import rose by 14% y-o-y in Sept.. In Sept. and Oct., some investors bought LME near dated contracts and sold SHFE futures contracts, which added imports. But as shrinking SHFE/LME arbitrage, refined copper imports might be affected. China’ refined copper export reached 2.39kt, down by 20% y-o-y. Due to recovering domestic copper demand, enterprises began rebuilding inventory. So refined copper exports will have a certain decline in the future. Copper scraps import reached 418.36kt in Sept, down by 2% y-o-y or up by 9% m-o-m. Domestic copper scrap supply was less and quality was also not good. Copper scrap import is in accordance with copper prices. It is expected copper scrap import will be at 400kt in Oct. As to copper concentrate, China’s copper concentrate import reached 562.33kt in Sept., down by 18% y-o-y and by about 17% m-o-m. Although copper concentrate import had a m-o-m decline, copper concentrate import in Sept was still higher more than that in the most months of H1 2011. That is to say, continuous high output of domestic refined copper stimulates copper concentrate import at a certain degree. It is estimated that copper concentrate import will keep at a similar level in Oct. _Source: the Customs_ Website: www.antaike.com 6 Copper Monthly No. 179 Source: the Customs
